Science 273(5280), published pp.1400-1401, Fig. 1/results: amnesic patients show preserved early classification acquisition with severely impaired declarative memory for the training episode

Science 273(5280), published pp.1400-1401, Fig. 1/results: Parkinson's disease patients fail to improve normally on early classification trials while retaining declarative memory for the training episode

conditions: neurological comparison groups with contrasting lesion or disease profiles
probabilistic classification training with cue combinations and two possible outcomes
post-training explicit assessment of the training episode
population: patients with frontal lobe lesions used to evaluate a frontal-dysfunction alternative
substrate: caudate nucleus and putamen affected in Parkinson's disease
task: probabilistic cue-combination classification across repeated trials
post-training multiple-choice questionnaire about the training episode
temporal_scope: classification acquisition is evaluated across repeated trial blocks; the early 50-trial phase is central to the neurological-group contrast
explicit report concerning the training episode is assessed after classification training

nodes.description: amnesic patient group with limbic-diencephalic damage and severe impairment in explicit report of the training episode
nondemented Parkinson's disease group with striatal dysfunction
frontal-lobe-lesion comparison group used to evaluate whether frontal dysfunction alone accounts for the classification deficit
repeated probabilistic cue-combination classification trials that provide the acquisition experience and yield blockwise performance measurements
gradual improvement or failure to improve in probabilistic classification accuracy across repeated trials
post-training multiple-choice test of explicit report concerning the training episode
measured explicit report concerning the training episode
classification performance evaluated relative to the task's probabilistic cue-outcome contingencies across trial blocks
source interpretation that the crossed classification/explicit-report pattern reflects separable parallel functional systems associated with limbic-diencephalic and striatal damage
caudate nucleus and putamen, implicated by the source in gradual incremental associative acquisition

relations.description: the repeated probabilistic classification sequence supplies the acquisition experience and the serial behavioral measure
the post-training questionnaire probes explicit report for the training episode
amnesic patients show preserved early probabilistic classification acquisition despite severely impaired explicit report for the training episode
Parkinson's disease patients fail to acquire the probabilistic classification task normally despite intact explicit report for the training episode
classification training precedes the explicit-report assessment of the training episode
acquisition is evaluated from classification accuracy over repeated trial blocks under the probabilistic cue-outcome structure
the crossed behavioral pattern is interpreted by the source as distinguishing separate and parallel learning systems
the frontal-lobe-lesion comparison performs satisfactorily relative to the Parkinson's disease deficit during the early classification phase, weakening a frontal-dysfunction-only explanation

the authors infer that the caudate nucleus and putamen is essential for gradual incremental associative acquisition; this is the source's causal interpretation of the clinical dissociation, not a randomized intervention on the caudate nucleus and putamen
